widgets.title: Question 1

prompt.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: C] be a simple, piecewise-smooth, closed, and positively oriented curve. Given that the line integral [MATH: ∮_(C)Pdx + Qdy] represents the area of the region [MATH: D] enclosed by any such curve in [MATH: R^{2},] which of the following could be the functions [MATH: P(x, y)] and [MATH: Q(x, y)?]

  1. [MATH: P(x, y) = y] and [MATH: Q(x, y) = − x]

  2. [MATH: P(x, y) = (x)/(2) + \cos y^{2}] and [MATH: Q(x, y) = (y)/(2)]

  3. [MATH: P(x, y) = 0] and [MATH: Q(x, y) = x]

widgets.title: Question 2

prompt.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: C] be a simple, piecewise-smooth, closed, and positively oriented curve. Given that the line integral [MATH: ∮_(C)F ⋅ dr] represents the area of the region [MATH: D] enclosed by any such curve in [MATH: R^{2},] which of the following could be the vector field [MATH: F(x, y)?]

  1. [MATH: F(x, y) = ⟨ − y, x^{2} + x⟩]

  2. [MATH: F(x, y) = ⟨ − (y)/(4) + x, (3x)/(4)⟩]

  3. [MATH: F(x, y) = ⟨ − y, 0⟩]
